findings.summary: GRASP provides matched causal support that candidate generation must not imply admission. On MedAgentBench/gpt-oss-120b, full GRASP reports 88.8% test accuracy, while removing only the acceptance gate and applying every proposed edit unconditionally reports 63.5% at K=4 and 40.1% at K=1. Matched-compute variants that run the probe but discard its verdict reach 70.8% and 67.2%. Rejected candidates explicitly leave the skill library unchanged.

GSEM's first inspected pre-submission public commit already contains an explicit GSEMMultiStartNoFillAgent and a dedicated no-fill retriever whose sole documented difference is preserving an empty result instead of force-filling the start node. The paper's published retrieval ablation omits this factor, and no bound numerical no-fill output was found, so this is design-factor evidence only.

protocol_inferences.name: PROPOSAL_GENERATION_DOES_NOT_IMPLY_ADMISSION
protocol_inferences.consequence: Keep a valid reject/no-retention path and require independent admission evidence before injection. No canonical validator mutation: memory_admission_runtime_v1 already implements the lifecycle distinction.

protocol_inferences.name: EMPTY_RETRIEVAL_IS_A_DESIGN_FACTOR_NOT_AN_EFFECT_CLAIM
protocol_inferences.consequence: Do not infer performance benefit from GSEM no-fill implementation existence without bound quantitative outputs.
